title: Why clutter stresses us out, with Dn. Joseph Ferrari, PhD

sentences.en: Do you sometimes feel overwhelmed by all of your stuff?
sentences.zh: 你有时会因为自己的东西太多而感到不知所措吗？

sentences.en: If so, you're not alone.
sentences.zh: 如果是这样，你并不孤单。

sentences.en: In recent years, a thriving decluttering industry has sprung up to help us all deal with our ever-accumulating piles of things.
sentences.zh: 近年来，一个蓬勃发展的“去杂物”行业应运而生，旨在帮助我们所有人处理不断堆积的物品。

sentences.en: The stacks of books that don't fit on our shelves, our kids' outgrown toys, our clothes that don't fit anymore, our overstuffed closets,
sentences.zh: 书架上放不下的书、孩子们玩剩下的玩具、不再合身的衣服、塞得满满当当的壁橱，

sentences.en: and our garages that are so full of clutter that they no longer fit our cars.
sentences.zh: 还有那些堆满杂物以至于连车都停不进去的车库。

sentences.en: How does all of this clutter affect us?
sentences.zh: 所有这些杂物是如何影响我们的呢？

sentences.en: In recent years, psychologist research has begun to find that living and working in cluttered spaces causes stress and anxiety and can harm both our mental
sentences.zh: 近年来，心理学研究开始发现，在杂乱的空间中生活和工作会引起压力和焦虑，并可能损害我们的心理

sentences.en: health and our productivity.
sentences.zh: 健康和生产力。

sentences.en: So why do we accumulate so much stuff and why do we find it so hard to deal with it?
sentences.zh: 那么，我们为什么会积累这么多东西，又为什么觉得处理它们如此困难呢？

sentences.en: Does everyone find clutter equally stressful or are some people happy living in spaces that might seem chaotic to others?
sentences.zh: 每个人都觉得杂乱会带来同样的压力吗？还是有些人乐于生活在别人看来可能很混乱的空间里？

sentences.en: What is clutter anyway and how is living in clutter different from hoarding?
sentences.zh: 到底什么是杂乱？生活在杂乱中与囤积症有什么区别？

sentences.en: Do men and women deal with clutter differently?
sentences.zh: 男性和女性处理杂乱的方式不同吗？

sentences.en: How does clutter affect relationships?
sentences.zh: 杂乱如何影响人际关系？

sentences.en: And if you want to clear the clutter in your home, what's the best way to get started and to stick with it?
sentences.zh: 如果你想清理家中的杂物，最好的开始方式是什么，又该如何坚持下去？

sentences.en: Welcome to Speaking of Psychology, the flagship podcast of the American
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《心理学谈话》，这是美国心理学会的旗舰播客，

sentences.en: Psychological Association that examines the links between psychological science and everyday life.
sentences.zh: 旨在探讨心理科学与日常生活之间的联系。

sentences.en: I'm Kim Mills.
sentences.zh: 我是金·米尔斯。

sentences.en: My guest today is Dr. Joseph Ferrari, a professor of psychology and distinguished professor at DePaul University in Chicago.
sentences.zh: 我今天的嘉宾是约瑟夫·法拉利博士，他是芝加哥德保罗大学的心理学教授和杰出教授。

sentences.en: Dr. Ferrari studies the psychology of clutter, including why we accumulate it, how it affects our mental health, and the link between clutter and procrastination.
sentences.zh: 法拉利博士研究杂乱的心理学，包括我们为什么会积累杂物、它如何影响我们的心理健康，以及杂乱与拖延症之间的联系。

sentences.en: He's also well known for his research on the causes and consequences of procrastination
sentences.zh: 他还因研究拖延症的成因和后果而闻名，

sentences.en: and is the author of several books on that subject for researchers, clinicians, and the general public.
sentences.zh: 并为研究人员、临床医生和大众撰写了多本相关主题的书籍。

sentences.en: He has published more than 400 scholarly articles and is a fellow in six professional organizations, including APA.
sentences.zh: 他发表了400多篇学术文章，是包括美国心理学会在内的六个专业组织的成员。

sentences.en: In addition to his work as a psychology professor, Dr. Ferrari is also a permanent deacon in the Catholic Diocese of Joliet, Illinois.
sentences.zh: 除了心理学教授的工作外，法拉利博士还是伊利诺伊州乔利埃特天主教教区的一名终身执事。

sentences.en: Thank you for joining me, Dr. Ferrari.
sentences.zh: 感谢您参加我们的节目，法拉利博士。

sentences.en: Well, first of all, thank you.
sentences.zh: 首先，谢谢你。

sentences.en: As I heard your introduction, it touched on a number of topics that I can begin to jump in and share with you if you'd like, such as the difference between clutter and hoarding.
sentences.zh: 刚才听到你的介绍，里面提到了很多话题，如果你愿意，我可以从这些话题切入并与你分享，比如杂乱与囤积的区别。

sentences.en: They're not the same.
sentences.zh: 它们并不相同。

sentences.en: As you know, hoarding is a psychological disorder.
sentences.zh: 如你所知，囤积症是一种心理障碍。

sentences.en: And the way I conceptualize this, and one of the ways to look at this is think of hoarding as lots of the same stuff,
sentences.zh: 我对此的构想，以及看待这个问题的一种方式是，把囤积看作是大量相同的东西，

sentences.en: toilet paper, toilet paper, toilet paper, toilet paper, and clutter is breadth.
sentences.zh: 比如卫生纸、卫生纸、卫生纸、卫生纸，而杂乱则是指广度。

sentences.en: So one is vertical and one is horizontal, if you would.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果可以这样比喻的话，一个是纵向的，一个是横向的。

sentences.en: So the person with clutter has lots of stuff.
sentences.zh: 所以，杂乱的人拥有很多不同的东西。

sentences.en: One of the other issues that you mentioned was, is it more common among one gender or the other?
sentences.zh: 你提到的另一个问题是，这种情况在某一性别中是否更常见？

sentences.en: All right, let me answer that by sharing some of the background.
sentences.zh: 好的，让我通过分享一些背景来回答这个问题。

sentences.en: In maybe a little over a decade ago, Dr. Catherine Roster from the
sentences.zh: 大约十多年前，来自新墨西哥大学的凯瑟琳·罗斯特博士和我参加了一个会议，

sentences.en: University of New Mexico and I were at a conference, an annual meeting for the members of ICD.
sentences.zh: 那是ICD成员的年度会议。

sentences.en: And so I'd like you listeners to reach out to your local ICD member.
sentences.zh: 所以我希望听众们能联系你们当地的ICD成员。

sentences.en: That stands for the Institute for Challenging
sentences.zh: 那代表的是“挑战性组织混乱研究所”。

sentences.en: Disorganization.
sentences.zh: （Institute for Challenging Disorganization）

sentences.en: They're the professional declutterers.
sentences.zh: 他们是专业的整理师。

sentences.en: They're the coaches that you would hire if you have a clutter issue.
sentences.zh: 如果你有杂乱问题，他们就是你会雇佣的教练。

sentences.en: They are the experts.
sentences.zh: 他们是专家。

sentences.en: Now, notice their organization.
sentences.zh: 现在，注意他们的组织名称。

sentences.en: It doesn't say the word clutter because for them, it's all an issue of disorganization.
sentences.zh: 里面没有“杂乱”这个词，因为对他们来说，这完全是一个组织混乱的问题。

sentences.en: And I'll explore more of that in a moment.
sentences.zh: 稍后我会深入探讨这一点。

sentences.en: But anyway, Roster and I were there.
sentences.zh: 总之，当时罗斯特和我都在那里。

sentences.en: I presented on procrastination.
sentences.zh: 我做了关于拖延症的演讲。

sentences.en: They wanted to know more.
sentences.zh: 他们想了解更多。

sentences.en: And afterwards, Catherine Roster comes to me and says, let's collaborate.
sentences.zh: 之后，凯瑟琳·罗斯特找到我说，我们合作吧。

sentences.en: And I said, great.
sentences.zh: 我说，太好了。

sentences.en: I want to study the psychological home.
sentences.zh: 我想研究“心理家园”。

sentences.en: That's another area.
sentences.zh: 那是另一个领域。

sentences.en: I'm a social community psychologist for listeners who are familiar.
sentences.zh: 对于熟悉的听众来说，我是一名社会社区心理学家。

sentences.en: And I'm interested in what is the meaning of home for people?
sentences.zh: 我对“家”对人们意味着什么很感兴趣。

sentences.en: We travel.
sentences.zh: 我们去旅行。

sentences.en: We can't wait to go home.
sentences.zh: 我们迫不及待地想回家。

sentences.en: You eat me out of house and home.
sentences.zh: 你把我的家底都吃光了。

sentences.en: Home is something different than a dwelling.
sentences.zh: “家”与“住所”是不同的概念。

sentences.en: And she said, sure, let's look at that.
sentences.zh: 她说，没问题，我们来看看这个。

sentences.en: Well, anyway, we collected our first study that came out in 2016 in the Journal of Environmental Psychology.
sentences.zh: 总之，我们收集了第一项研究数据，并于2016年发表在《环境心理学杂志》上。

sentences.en: And that data had about 1,800, 1,600 adults, but only 50 men.
sentences.zh: 那份数据大约有1800到1600名成年人，但只有50名男性。

sentences.en: And so, the first thing I did is I contacted the ICD people and said, wait a minute, is this skewed?
sentences.zh: 所以，我做的第一件事就是联系ICD的人说，等一下，这有偏差吗？

sentences.en: Is there a gender difference?
sentences.zh: 存在性别差异吗？

sentences.en: And they said, no, no, no, no.
sentences.zh: 他们说，不，不，不，不。

sentences.en: Men have clutter, but they don't see it as clutter.
sentences.zh: 男性也有杂物，但他们不认为那是杂乱。

sentences.en: For men, it's my toys.
sentences.zh: 对男性来说，那是“我的玩具”。

sentences.en: It's my stuff.
sentences.zh: 那是“我的东西”。

sentences.en: For women, our culture tells them, you've got clutter.
sentences.zh: 对女性来说，我们的文化告诉她们：你有杂乱问题。

sentences.en: So, that's very interesting.
sentences.zh: 所以，这非常有趣。

sentences.en: So, the experts will tell you there is no gender difference, even though one may go seek assistance and the other one doesn't.
sentences.zh: 因此，专家会告诉你不存在性别差异，尽管一方可能会寻求帮助，而另一方则不会。

sentences.en: So, when does clutter become a problem for people?
sentences.zh: 那么，杂乱在什么时候会成为人们的问题呢？

sentences.en: Why do some people find it stressful and other people can live in the middle of it and they're fine?
sentences.zh: 为什么有些人觉得它压力很大，而另一些人却能生活在其中并安之若素？

sentences.en: Yep, yep, yep.
sentences.zh: 没错，没错，没错。

sentences.en: There's a tip and point, like so many things in life.
sentences.zh: 就像生活中的许多事情一样，有一个临界点。

sentences.en: It's when does it become procrastination and not just delay?
sentences.zh: 就像什么时候它变成了拖延症，而不仅仅是延迟？

sentences.en: You know, there's a point where things switch over from one to the other.
sentences.zh: 你知道，事物从一种状态转变为另一种状态有一个临界点。

sentences.en: The way Catherine
sentences.zh: 凯瑟琳·罗斯特和我根据我们2016年的论文对杂乱的定义是：

sentences.en: Roster and I define a clutter based on our 2016 paper is it's an overabundance of possessions that collectively can create chaos and disorderly living spaces.
sentences.zh: 它是过剩的财产，集体起来会造成混乱和无序的生活空间。

sentences.en: That's a mouthful.
sentences.zh: 这听起来很拗口。

sentences.en: I'm reading to you all right, but this may answer your question.
sentences.zh: 我是在照本宣科，但这可能回答了你的问题。

sentences.en: Overabundance.
sentences.zh: 过剩。

sentences.en: There's just too much.
sentences.zh: 就是东西太多了。

sentences.en: You mentioned a moment ago, I'm a Catholic clergy.
sentences.zh: 你刚才提到，我是天主教神职人员。

sentences.en: I am a deacon.
sentences.zh: 我是一名执事。

sentences.en: And if I may for the moment, we're not called to live as paupers.
sentences.zh: 如果可以的话，我们并不被要求像乞丐一样生活。

sentences.en: Christ never tells you that, to do that.
sentences.zh: 基督从未告诉你要那样做。

sentences.en: He said the problem isn't abundance, it's attachment to the abundance.
sentences.zh: 他说问题不在于丰盛，而在于对丰盛的执着。

sentences.en: That's the problem.
sentences.zh: 那才是问题所在。

sentences.en: We don't let go.
sentences.zh: 我们不肯放手。

sentences.en: So, we have this overabundance of things and it really creates a chaotic life and disorderly living.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们拥有过剩的东西，这确实创造了一种混乱的生活和无序的居住环境。

sentences.en: So, from this, Roster and I have identified four areas where we look at clutter when we do these studies.
sentences.zh: 因此，基于此，罗斯特和我在进行这些研究时，确定了四个观察杂乱的领域。

sentences.en: Livability of the space.
sentences.zh: 空间的可居住性。

sentences.en: Does the amount of stuff you have impact your livability?
sentences.zh: 你拥有的东西数量会影响你的可居住性吗？

sentences.en: You can't manage the physical space.
sentences.zh: 你无法管理物理空间。

sentences.en: Does it cause you distress?
sentences.zh: 它会给你带来困扰吗？

sentences.en: Is there emotional consequences from this?
sentences.zh: 这会带来情感后果吗？

sentences.en: By having it, is there too much?
sentences.zh: 拥有这些东西，是不是太多了？

sentences.en: And it really distresses your life.
sentences.zh: 它确实让你的生活感到痛苦。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Readers and listeners and readers of my work will find that we found that there's a negative correlation between life satisfaction and clutter.
sentences.zh: 读者和听众，以及我作品的读者会发现，我们发现生活满意度与杂乱之间存在负相关。

sentences.en: So, the more clutter you have, the lower people report life satisfaction, greater distress.
sentences.zh: 所以，你拥有的杂物越多，人们报告的生活满意度就越低，痛苦感就越强。

sentences.en: So, here we live in this consumer culture, but more and more and more, buy, buy, buy.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们生活在这种消费文化中，但越来越多，买、买、买。

sentences.en: Well, you're actually not living a good, complete life because you'll be less satisfied.
sentences.zh: 好吧，你实际上并没有过上美好、完整的生活，因为你会感到不那么满足。

sentences.en: A third area is it impacts relationships.
sentences.zh: 第三个领域是它影响人际关系。

sentences.en: We'll talk about in a few minutes.
sentences.zh: 我们几分钟后再谈。

sentences.en: Why is it so hard to get rid of things?
sentences.zh: 为什么摆脱东西这么难？

sentences.en: Because often we're not the only owner.
sentences.zh: 因为通常我们不是唯一的拥有者。

sentences.en: There's often someone else.
sentences.zh: 通常还有别人。

sentences.en: So, it impacts relationships, causes lots of stress.
sentences.zh: 所以，它会影响人际关系，造成很大的压力。

sentences.en: And of course, financial well-being.
sentences.zh: 当然，还有财务状况。

sentences.en: There's a study that was done that showed Americans have over
sentences.zh: 有一项研究表明，美国人房子里有超过

sentences.en: $7,000 of unused stuff in their house.
sentences.zh: 7000美元的闲置物品。

sentences.en: It's a lot.
sentences.zh: 这很多。

sentences.en: And then we wonder why people are a paycheck away from, you know, being on the streets.
sentences.zh: 然后我们奇怪为什么人们离流落街头只差一个月的工资。

sentences.en: Why credit cards are maxed out.
sentences.zh: 为什么信用卡会刷爆。

sentences.en: Did you need $7,000 worth of stuff?
sentences.zh: 你真的需要价值7000美元的东西吗？

sentences.en: And then I know you want to ask a question, but one more thing for the listener.
sentences.zh: 我知道你想问一个问题，但还有一件事要告诉听众。

sentences.en: The three areas that ICD members and we found that people have the most clutter is in the kitchen, in the closet, and books.
sentences.zh: ICD成员和我们发现人们杂物最多的三个地方是厨房、壁橱和书架。

sentences.en: So, let me ask you this.
sentences.zh: 那么，让我问你这个。

sentences.en: Where does the propensity to clutter come from?
sentences.zh: 杂乱的倾向从何而来？

sentences.en: Is it something that emerges in childhood or do you become a clutterer as an adult?
sentences.zh: 它是童年时期出现的，还是成年后才变得杂乱？

sentences.en: And is it learned so that if you had parents who maybe were tolerant of stuff or were cluttery themselves, does that make you a clutterer or not?
sentences.zh: 它是后天习得的吗？如果你的父母可能对杂物比较宽容，或者他们自己就很杂乱，这会让你也变得杂乱吗？

sentences.en: You didn't say, and are you born a clutterer?
sentences.zh: 你没说，你是天生就杂乱吗？

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 不。

sentences.en: You know, we're psychologists here and we know that 98%, at least I was always taught, of who you are comes from learning.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们是心理学家，我们知道至少我一直被教导，你98%的性格来自于学习。

sentences.en: You know, the 2% is the biological.
sentences.zh: 你知道，2%是生物性的。

sentences.en: But we turn so much today for the biological base of things.
sentences.zh: 但今天我们太倾向于从生物学基础来看待事物了。

sentences.en: So, there's no biology behind clutter.
sentences.zh: 所以，杂乱背后没有生物学依据。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: At least nobody has published that.
sentences.zh: 至少没有人发表过相关研究。

sentences.en: But the answer to your question is we don't know.
sentences.zh: 但你问题的答案是：我们不知道。

sentences.en: You're talking to half the scholars in the field.
sentences.zh: 你正在和该领域一半的学者交谈。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: And knowing the other half, she doesn't look at it.
sentences.zh: 而了解另一半学者的情况，她并没有研究这个。

sentences.en: We have to look at that topic.
sentences.zh: 我们必须研究这个课题。

sentences.en: I'm hoping someone's listening and say, oh, there's my dissertation.
sentences.zh: 我希望有人在听，然后说，哦，这就是我的博士论文题目。

sentences.en: Ah, there's my, you know, master's thesis.
sentences.zh: 啊，这就是我的硕士论文。

sentences.en: Oh, there's the honors thesis as an undergrad.
sentences.zh: 哦，这就是本科的荣誉论文。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对的。

sentences.en: Come join me at DePaul.
sentences.zh: 来德保罗大学加入我吧。

sentences.en: We'll do some great research together.
sentences.zh: 我们将一起做一些伟大的研究。

sentences.en: The point is we don't know the development.
sentences.zh: 重点是我们不知道它的发展过程。

sentences.en: Where does it come from?
sentences.zh: 它从哪里来？

sentences.en: I mean,
sentences.zh: 我是说，

sentences.en: I'd love to look at minimalists, the complete opposite of the clutterer.
sentences.zh: 我很想研究极简主义者，他们是杂乱者的完全对立面。

sentences.en: Don't know.
sentences.zh: 不知道。

sentences.en: Don't have any data on that, that we know of.
sentences.zh: 据我们所知，没有任何关于这方面的数据。

sentences.en: There were people who in the seventies who looked at
sentences.zh: 七十年代有人研究过

sentences.en: snooping was the name of a book where people would look at people's possessions, but never in the point of clutter.
sentences.zh: 《窥探》是一本书的名字，人们会查看别人的财物，但从未从杂乱的角度进行研究。

sentences.en: And again, I want people to understand we're not talking hoarding.
sentences.zh: 再次强调，我希望大家明白，我们讨论的不是囤积症。

sentences.en: The TV show is called hoarders, right?
sentences.zh: 电视节目叫《囤积者》，对吧？

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: It's not called clutterers.
sentences.zh: 它不叫《杂物堆积者》。

sentences.en: It's different.
sentences.zh: 这是两码事。

sentences.en: And again, as the,
sentences.zh: 再说一次，正如

sentences.en: ICD people would say, if it doesn't impact your life, if you're happy with having all that stuff, okay.
sentences.zh: ICD（挑战性无序研究所）的人会说的那样，如果它没有影响你的生活，如果你对拥有这些东西感到快乐，那没问题。

sentences.en: It's only when it impacts financially relationships, like anything in life, you need to deal something with it.
sentences.zh: 只有当它在经济上或人际关系上造成影响时，就像生活中的任何事情一样，你才需要去处理它。

sentences.en: So why is it so hard for people to declutter?
sentences.zh: 那么，为什么人们清理杂物会这么难呢？

sentences.en: I mean, when you recognize that maybe it's taking over your life, but how do you get started?
sentences.zh: 我是说，当你意识到它可能正在占据你的生活时，该如何开始呢？

sentences.en: And I want to ask you about the whole Marie Kondo notion that we should keep the things that give us joy, right?
sentences.zh: 我想问问你关于近藤麻理惠的那个观点，即我们应该保留那些能给我们带来“心动”感觉的东西，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean,
sentences.zh: 我是说，

sentences.en: I know you have views around that.
sentences.zh: 我知道你对此有自己的看法。

sentences.en: Why is it so hard to declutter?
sentences.zh: 为什么清理杂物这么难？

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: Let me give you a few reasons.
sentences.zh: 让我给你几个理由。

sentences.en: One, the items could be emotionally stressful.
sentences.zh: 第一，物品可能会带来情感上的压力。

sentences.en: Now, not only negatively, as you're probably thought by those words, but could be positive.
sentences.zh: 这种压力不仅是负面的——正如你可能从这些词中想到的那样——也可能是正面的。

sentences.en: That is to say, it could be a trigger.
sentences.zh: 也就是说，它可能是一个触发点。

sentences.en: When I pick the item up, all right, it might bring me joy or happiness.
sentences.zh: 当我拿起这件东西时，它可能会带给我喜悦或快乐。

sentences.en: Happiness, not joy.
sentences.zh: 是快乐，不是心动。

sentences.en: I may look at it and say, oh, I remember that good time we had.
sentences.zh: 我看着它可能会说，哦，我记得我们当时度过的美好时光。

sentences.en: I got to keep that.
sentences.zh: 我得留着它。

sentences.en: Or I pick it up and I say, oh yes, that was, that was a really tough time in my life.
sentences.zh: 或者我拿起它时说，哦，是的，那是我生命中一段非常艰难的时期。

sentences.en: That was some relationship.
sentences.zh: 那是一段复杂的关系。

sentences.en: And I want to avoid it.
sentences.zh: 我想避开它。

sentences.en: So it could be a trigger to something in the paSt. And that's one of the reasons it's harder to declutter because it brings back either positive or negative emotions.
sentences.zh: 所以它可能是过去某件事的触发点。这就是清理杂物更难的原因之一，因为它会勾起正面或负面的情绪。

sentences.en: Again, another line of research could be, well, when is it one or the other?
sentences.zh: 再说一次，另一个研究方向可能是，嗯，什么时候是正面，什么时候是负面？

sentences.en: How can we predict?
sentences.zh: 我们该如何预测？

sentences.en: That'd be great.
sentences.zh: 那会很棒。

sentences.en: Also, it's hard to declutter because there are, as I said a few minutes ago, multiple users.
sentences.zh: 此外，清理杂物很难，因为正如我几分钟前所说，这里涉及多个使用者。

sentences.en: Most of the time, the decision to keep or get rid of something is not just my own.
sentences.zh: 大多数时候，保留或丢弃某样东西的决定不仅仅是我自己的。

sentences.en: Perhaps you have a partner.
sentences.zh: 也许你有伴侣。

sentences.en: Perhaps you're living with someone.
sentences.zh: 也许你和别人住在一起。

sentences.en: Perhaps there's someone else, others in your life.
sentences.zh: 也许你的生活中还有其他人。

sentences.en: And so you want to throw it away, but the other people say, no, we need to keep it.
sentences.zh: 所以你想把它扔掉，但其他人会说，不，我们需要留着它。

sentences.en: So it may not be your own decision and getting rid of it would cause a conflict.
sentences.zh: 所以这可能不是你个人的决定，丢掉它会引发冲突。

sentences.en: And then the three lacks, I call it the three lacks, lack of time, lack of resources and lack of ability, lack of time.
sentences.zh: 还有“三个缺乏”，我称之为“三个缺乏”：缺乏时间、缺乏资源和缺乏能力。首先是缺乏时间。

sentences.en: People say, yeah, this is great.
sentences.zh: 人们会说，太棒了。

sentences.en: They're listening to you today, us today.
sentences.zh: 他们今天在听你讲，听我们讲。

sentences.en: And they're saying, yeah, this is great.
sentences.zh: 他们会说，太棒了。

sentences.en: But as I talk about in my book, problem procrastination, the but however factor people, we are great excuse makers.
sentences.zh: 但正如我在书中谈到的拖延问题，人们总有“但是”这个因素，我们非常擅长找借口。

sentences.en: I would, I'd love to do it, but I don't have time.
sentences.zh: 我愿意做，我很想做，但我没时间。

sentences.en: Well, that sparked a study by Roster and I during COVID.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这引发了我和Roster在新冠疫情期间的一项研究。

sentences.en: Now you're locked up.
sentences.zh: 现在你被封锁了。

sentences.en: Now you can't go anywhere.
sentences.zh: 现在你哪儿也去不了。

sentences.en: Now you have the time.
sentences.zh: 现在你有时间了。

sentences.en: Do you declutter?
sentences.zh: 你清理杂物了吗？

sentences.en: So we went to the ICD experts, their board of directors and stuff, and did a focus group before we launched our study.
sentences.zh: 所以我们找到了ICD的专家，他们的董事会成员等等，在开展研究之前进行了一次焦点小组讨论。

sentences.en: And we said, what do you think?
sentences.zh: 我们问，你们怎么看？

sentences.en: Are people, and they're saying, oh yeah, our clients always said, I'd love to declutter more, but I can't.
sentences.zh: 人们……他们说，哦，是的，我们的客户总是说，我很想多清理些杂物，但我做不到。

sentences.en: And now they're home and they're not.
sentences.zh: 现在他们待在家里，却依然没有清理。

sentences.en: That that's an excuse.
sentences.zh: 那……那是个借口。

sentences.en: That is yet another, because now that we're forced to be home, we don't.
sentences.zh: 那又是另一个借口，因为现在我们被迫待在家里，我们还是没做。

sentences.en: Now Roster and I collected data and we have an article coming out in the Journal of
sentences.zh: 现在，我和Roster收集了数据，我们有一篇文章即将发表在《消费者事务杂志》上，

sentences.en: Consumer Affairs, should be coming out shortly.
sentences.zh: 应该很快就会出来。

sentences.en: I know it's online already, where we find three types of people during COVID who decluttered.
sentences.zh: 我知道它已经在网上了，我们在文中发现了疫情期间清理杂物的三类人。

sentences.en: There were some who found it was exciting and energetic and loved it.
sentences.zh: 有些人觉得这很令人兴奋、充满活力，并且乐在其中。

sentences.en: There were some who found it as, well, it's something I got to do, but I don't enjoy it.
sentences.zh: 有些人觉得，嗯，这是我必须做的事，但我并不享受。

sentences.en: And then there was the other ones who just didn't declutter.
sentences.zh: 还有一类人根本就没有清理。

sentences.en: And those last two groups were much higher than the small group who enjoyed decluttering.
sentences.zh: 而后两类人的比例远高于那些享受清理杂物的小群体。

sentences.en: So lack of time, a lack of resources.
sentences.zh: 所以，缺乏时间，缺乏资源。

sentences.en: People will say, I'd love to get rid of it, but I don't know what to do with it.
sentences.zh: 人们会说，我很想把它处理掉，但我不知道该怎么处理。

sentences.en: Where am I going to go with it?
sentences.zh: 我能把它送到哪儿去呢？

sentences.en: My kids don't want the China.
sentences.zh: 我的孩子们不想要这些瓷器。

sentences.en: I can't get rid of the old furniture and stuff like that.
sentences.zh: 我没法处理掉旧家具之类的东西。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: Again, good excuse making.
sentences.zh: 同样，这是很好的借口。

sentences.en: My God, there are so many sources out there that are dying for resources.
sentences.zh: 天哪，外面有那么多机构正急需这些资源。

sentences.en: In my area here in the Joliet Diocese, there's an organization that will take your furniture and put it into a home of a new family who may need it.
sentences.zh: 在我所在的乔利埃特教区，有一个组织会接收你的家具，并将其放入可能需要它的新家庭的家中。

sentences.en: I'm thinking of the ones we donated.
sentences.zh: 我想到的是我们捐赠的那些家具。

sentences.en: There was a woman whose husband was abusive.
sentences.zh: 曾有一位女性，她的丈夫有虐待行为。

sentences.en: She finally left him.
sentences.zh: 她最终离开了丈夫。

sentences.en: They helped set up an apartment for the woman and her kids.
sentences.zh: 他们帮助这位女性和她的孩子们布置了一个公寓。

sentences.en: And we donated some of our furniture as our kids have moved on.
sentences.zh: 随着我们的孩子搬走，我们也捐赠了一些家具。

sentences.en: So your family doesn't want it.
sentences.zh: 所以，你的家人不想要它。

sentences.en: Other families may want it.
sentences.zh: 其他家庭可能需要它。

sentences.en: Yes, exactly.
sentences.zh: 是的，完全正确。

sentences.en: You know, you read in the paper, somebody's house has burned down.
sentences.zh: 你知道，你在报纸上读到，某人的房子被烧毁了。

sentences.en: A flood has hit over there.
sentences.zh: 那边发生了洪水。

sentences.en: They don't want your China, your kids.
sentences.zh: 他们不想要你的瓷器，你的孩子们也不要。

sentences.en: But that family would love to have those dishes.
sentences.zh: 但那个家庭会很乐意拥有那些餐具。

sentences.en: So leave a legacy, is what I say in my ministry.
sentences.zh: 所以，留下遗产，这是我在我的事工中常说的。

sentences.en: Leave a legacy.
sentences.zh: 留下遗产。

sentences.en: Make a difference in other people's lives.
sentences.zh: 对他人的生活产生影响。

sentences.en: It may not be your own families, but in others.
sentences.zh: 可能不是你自己的家庭，而是其他人。

sentences.en: Lack of time, lack of resources, and lack of ability.
sentences.zh: 缺乏时间、缺乏资源和缺乏能力。

sentences.en: Many people say they don't know what to do.
sentences.zh: 许多人说他们不知道该怎么办。

sentences.en: That's where the decluttering coaches come in.
sentences.zh: 这就是清理教练发挥作用的地方。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: They're not necessarily psychologists.
sentences.zh: 他们不一定是心理学家。

sentences.en: They may not necessarily even have a master's degree, but they're just people who are trained.
sentences.zh: 他们甚至不一定有硕士学位，但他们只是受过训练的人。

sentences.en: The ICD group does lots of certifications for people who know how to organize and declutter, which takes me to the quote you gave me.
sentences.zh: ICD组织为那些懂得如何整理和清理的人提供了大量的认证，这让我想到了你给我的那句名言。

sentences.en: Touch it and keep it if it gives you joy.
sentences.zh: “触摸它，如果它给你带来心动，就留下它。”

sentences.en: Well, I struggle with that quote.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我对这句话有异议。

sentences.en: Let's look at the data.
sentences.zh: 让我们看看数据。

sentences.en: You know, we're scientists here.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们是科学家。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对吧。

sentences.en: Consumer psychologists, as Roster has taught me, will tell you, if you touch something in the store, you're more likely to buy it.
sentences.zh: 正如Roster教我的，消费者心理学家会告诉你，如果你在商店里触摸了某样东西，你更有可能买下它。

sentences.en: You're more likely to keep it.
sentences.zh: 你更有可能保留它。

sentences.en: And that is the reason why retailers, companies in stores will put things eye-level for you so that you can see it and you can buy it.
sentences.zh: 这就是零售商和商店里的公司把东西放在你视线平齐的位置的原因，这样你就能看到它，并买下它。

sentences.en: They pay extra to be eye-level than to be lower or higher.
sentences.zh: 他们宁愿多花钱放在视线平齐处，也不愿放在更低或更高的位置。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: So they want you to touch the item.
sentences.zh: 所以他们想让你触摸这些物品。

sentences.en: If you touch it, you're more likely to buy it.
sentences.zh: 如果你触摸了它，你就更有可能买下它。

sentences.en: So you're more likely to keep it.
sentences.zh: 所以你也就更有可能保留它。

sentences.en: The decluttering coaches would say to you, don't run out and buy a bin and start throwing stuff in the bin.
sentences.zh: 清理教练会告诉你，不要跑出去买个箱子，然后开始往里面扔东西。

sentences.en: Organize.
sentences.zh: 要整理。

sentences.en: That's why they're called the Institute for Challenging Disorganization.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么他们被称为“挑战性无序研究所”。

sentences.en: Organize and look and see, wow, I have six bachelors.
sentences.zh: 整理一下，看看，哇，我有六个搅拌机。

sentences.en: Jeez, 15 pairs of blue pants.
sentences.zh: 天哪，15条蓝色裤子。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: Look at all these things that I have.
sentences.zh: 看看我拥有的这些东西。

sentences.en: And then you bring in a coach or a good friend and they have them hold it.
sentences.zh: 然后你请来一位教练或好朋友，让他们拿着这些东西。

sentences.en: Because if they have found, if I touch it as the client, I'm more likely to keep that pair of pants.
sentences.zh: 因为他们发现，如果作为客户的我触摸了它，我更有可能留下那条裤子。

sentences.en: So the data and the experts say, don't touch it.
sentences.zh: 所以数据和专家都说，不要触摸它。

sentences.en: When this first hit the press and there was a
sentences.zh: 当这件事最初见诸报端，并且有一个

sentences.en: Netflix show on all of this, a lot of reporters came to me and said, what do you think?
sentences.zh: Netflix节目专门讲这些时，很多记者来找我问，你怎么看？

sentences.en: I remember talking to a Japanese reporter who said, what do you think of this expression?
sentences.zh: 我记得曾与一位日本记者交谈，他问，你觉得这个表达方式怎么样？

sentences.en: And I said, you know, I got to tell you the first half I told them, I said, but this, this joy, joy is a deep emotion, right?
sentences.zh: 我说，你知道，我得告诉你，我告诉了他们前半部分，我说，但这……这“心动”，心动是一种深层的情感，对吧？

sentences.en: Listeners, you know, this as psychology listeners, joy is not the same as happiness.
sentences.zh: 听众们，你们知道，作为心理学听众，心动（Joy）和快乐（Happiness）是不一样的。

sentences.en: Happiness is a mood.
sentences.zh: 快乐是一种情绪（Mood）。

sentences.en: Emotions are deeper.
sentences.zh: 情感（Emotions）更深层。

sentences.en: You know, we sing every Christmas joy to the world, not happiness to the world.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们每年圣诞节都唱“普世欢腾”（Joy to the world），而不是“普世快乐”。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: So there's something more to it there.
sentences.zh: 所以这里面还有更深层的含义。

sentences.en: And the Japanese reporter said, you know, you're right.
sentences.zh: 那位日本记者说，你知道，你是对的。

sentences.en: In Japanese, the word is happiness.
sentences.zh: 在日语中，这个词的意思是“快乐”。

sentences.en: It's been translated to joy because joy sells books.
sentences.zh: 它被翻译成了“心动”，因为“心动”能卖书。

sentences.en: So I got issues with this expression.
sentences.zh: 所以我对这个表达方式有意见。

sentences.en: Don't touch it.
sentences.zh: 不要触摸它。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: If it gives you momentary happiness, okay.
sentences.zh: 如果它给你带来短暂的快乐，那没问题。

sentences.en: But keep what gives you joy.
sentences.zh: 但要保留那些真正让你心动的东西。

sentences.en: What's deep.
sentences.zh: 那才是深层的。

sentences.en: You don't need 18 snow globes.
sentences.zh: 你不需要18个雪花球。

sentences.en: Maybe you can get away with four, three, you know, less.
sentences.zh: 也许四个、三个，你知道，少一点就够了。

sentences.en: You don't need every piece of artwork your kids did for you.
sentences.zh: 你不需要保留孩子们为你做的每一件艺术品。

sentences.en: Maybe you could pick up the key one of each age or something like that.
sentences.zh: 也许你可以挑选每个年龄段最关键的一件，或者类似的东西。

sentences.en: You know, again, no one's saying live like a pauper.
sentences.zh: 你知道，再说一次，没人说要像穷人一样生活。

sentences.en: You know, the Hindu monks, monks spend seven years getting rid of everything they own, except for two robes, two bowls, and two spoons.
sentences.zh: 你知道，印度僧侣花七年时间摆脱他们拥有的一切，只留下两件长袍、两个碗和两把勺子。

sentences.en: Try going on a cruise with just that.
sentences.zh: 试着只带这些去坐游轮看看。

sentences.en: It's impossible.
sentences.zh: 那是不可能的。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: We keep too much, but we're in this consumer society.
sentences.zh: 我们保留了太多东西，但我们身处这个消费社会。

sentences.en: Buy, buy, buy.
sentences.zh: 买，买，买。

sentences.en: More, more, more.
sentences.zh: 更多，更多，更多。

sentences.en: Got to have the lateSt. Got to have the new, the neweSt. What's happened is we've made our, our wants, needs.
sentences.zh: 必须拥有最新的。必须拥有新的，最新的。发生的事情是我们把我们的“想要”变成了“需要”。

sentences.en: We've made what we want to have as you gotta have.
sentences.zh: 我们把我们想要拥有的东西变成了你必须拥有的东西。

sentences.en: It's a need.
sentences.zh: 这成了一种需求。

sentences.en: And if you don't have it, oh, you're not, you know, you're not fine.
sentences.zh: 如果你没有这些东西，噢，你就不行了，你知道，你就没法过下去了。

sentences.en: You're not perfect.
sentences.zh: 你不够完美。

sentences.en: Let me switch to digital clutter because I know that's something that you've started studying.
sentences.zh: 让我转到数字杂物的话题上，因为我知道你已经开始研究这个了。

sentences.en: And so these files and documents and photos and emails that we all have clogging up our computers
sentences.zh: 我们电脑里塞满了各种文件、文档、照片和电子邮件，

sentences.en: and our, our cloud drives, does that kind of clutter affect us the same way emotionally, psychologically as the physical stuff?
sentences.zh: 还有我们的云端硬盘，这种杂物在情感和心理上对我们的影响，和实体杂物一样吗？

sentences.en: Currently, we've moved beyond the, um, looking at clutter in the home.
sentences.zh: 目前，我们已经不仅仅局限于观察家庭中的杂物了。

sentences.en: We have a number of studies of clutter in the office that we did, uh, pre pandemic, but we published it during the pandemic.
sentences.zh: 我们在疫情前做过一些关于办公室杂物的研究，不过是在疫情期间发表的。

sentences.en: One can find those articles.
sentences.zh: 大家可以找到这些文章。

sentences.en: And so then we've moved into now e-waste and digital clutter.
sentences.zh: 所以我们现在已经转向了电子垃圾和数字杂物领域。

sentences.en: So you ask a good question by e-waste.
sentences.zh: 你问电子垃圾这个问题问得很好。

sentences.en: I mean, electronic waste, how many old laptops and cell phones and the old wires that you might have and desktops on average,
sentences.zh: 我是说电子垃圾，平均来说，你有多少旧笔记本电脑、手机、旧电线和台式机？

sentences.en: there's a Swedish company that found on average, people have three cell phones, old cell phones on average that they don't use anymore.
sentences.zh: 有一家瑞典公司发现，人们平均有三部不再使用的旧手机。

sentences.en: So we've started to look at what impact does that have?
sentences.zh: 所以我们开始研究这会产生什么影响。

sentences.en: Again, as a social community psychologist, I see that relevant to climate and climate control and things.
sentences.zh: 作为一名社会社区心理学家，我认为这与气候、气候控制等问题息息相关。

sentences.en: How do, how does it impact my community, my setting, my, my area of living?
sentences.zh: 它如何影响我的社区、我的环境、我的生活区域？

sentences.en: Um, so we're starting to do that.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们正开始做这方面的研究。

sentences.en: So we need to be briefer and more succinct, I guess, in some of these things, but yes, we have to learn what's going on.

sentences.en: What she has found off the top of, hat off the press that she'll be presenting at the Eastern Psychological

sentences.en: Association conference, um, along with my team in Boston this year.
sentences.zh: 和我在波士顿的团队一起展示这些成果。

sentences.en: Um, what she found is that they do have clutter, but it's always, see, it's a question of perception too.
sentences.zh: 嗯，她发现他们确实有杂物，但你看，这同样是一个认知问题。

sentences.en: To many people, it's not my clutter.

sentences.en: Uh, and what do we do whenever they come to visit, they have to take something from their bedroom back home, right?
sentences.zh: 嗯，每当他们回来探亲时，我们都会让他们从卧室带走一些东西回家，对吧？

sentences.en: Just one thing, just one thing.

sentences.en: The other thing is when Christmas time comes, all right, she will buy something new for them, of course, but she'll look for something

sentences.en: in the house that's gently used and that's related to that.
sentences.zh: 保存完好且与他们相关的东西。

sentences.en: It's another way.
sentences.zh: 这是另一种方式。

sentences.en: So there's slow ways we can get rid of things because we have to learn to do that.
sentences.zh: 所以我们可以通过缓慢的方式处理掉东西，因为我们必须学会这样做。

sentences.en: You know, it's easy to accumulate.
sentences.zh: 你知道，积累东西很容易。

sentences.en: Is there generational differences?
sentences.zh: 有代际差异吗？

sentences.en: I would suspect probably because, you know, I have three kids and my son's the minimalist, but I don't use it in six, four to six months.
sentences.zh: 我怀疑可能有，因为，你知道，我有三个孩子，我儿子是个极简主义者，如果四到六个月不用，

sentences.en: I get rid of it.

sentences.zh: 所以我认为确实存在差异。

sentences.en: a professional, how should they approach getting rid of stuff?

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.zh: 这数量很多，但你知道，当你看着它们时，你会想，哇，我有这么多裤子。

sentences.en: Now, one thing you'll say to yourself is, well, maybe the hope, you know, hope runs eternal.

sentences.en: And then I would have a decluttering coach from my local area talk about the last half, how to declutter.

sentences.en: And I learned lots of good stuff.

sentences.zh: 这就是为什么她总是说，不要去买盒子、收纳箱，先分类整理，然后问问自己，你需要这个吗？

sentences.en: And one of the examples she always gave was every Thanksgiving, she needs this particular cookware thing, right?
sentences.zh: 她总是给出的例子之一是，每年感恩节，她都需要这件特定的厨具，对吧？

sentences.en: And so you rotate it around.

sentences.zh: 我们可以有创意一点。

sentences.zh: 我们可以做到这些。

sentences.en: Cognitive behavior therapy is what works most, CBT, if you're a procrastinator.
sentences.zh: 如果你有拖延症，认知行为疗法（CBT）才是最有效的。

sentences.en: So it's an interesting link between procrastination and clutter, and we've published a few studies on that.
sentences.zh: 所以拖延症和杂物堆积之间的联系很有趣，我们已经发表了一些关于这方面的研究。

sentences.en: One form of procrastination is decisional procrastination.
sentences.zh: 拖延症的一种形式是决策型拖延。

sentences.en: That's the cognitive form.
sentences.zh: 那是认知层面的形式。

sentences.en: Indecision is an interesting strategy that people use because I did some publications, experimental studies, looking at is it a cognitive deficit?
sentences.zh: 优柔寡断是一种人们常用的有趣策略，因为我做过一些出版物和实验研究，探讨这是否是一种认知缺陷？

sentences.en: Is it that people who are indecisive just can't make the decision or is it motivational?
sentences.zh: 是优柔寡断的人真的无法做决定，还是动机问题？

sentences.en: And of course, a variety of tasks, it came up motivational.
sentences.zh: 当然，在各种任务中，结果都指向了动机。

sentences.en: So people choose to be indecisive, all right?
sentences.zh: 所以人们是选择优柔寡断的，对吧？

sentences.en: But it's a great strategy.
sentences.zh: 但这确实是个好策略。

sentences.en: Let's take an example.
sentences.zh: 我们举个例子。

sentences.en: I live in the western suburbs of Chicago, outside of Naperville and Aurora, Illinois.
sentences.zh: 我住在芝加哥西郊，伊利诺伊州的内珀维尔和奥罗拉外围。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: And in Aurora, there's a
sentences.zh: 在奥罗拉，有一家

sentences.en: 31 movie multiplex.
sentences.zh: 31个放映厅的电影院。

sentences.en: 31 movies.
sentences.zh: 31部电影。

sentences.en: Now, imagine you go to the movie with your indecisive friend and you stand there with 31 options.
sentences.zh: 现在，想象一下你和优柔寡断的朋友去看电影，面对31个选择站在那里。

sentences.en: What will they tell you?
sentences.zh: 他们会跟你说什么？

sentences.en: You say, come on, we got to pick a movie.
sentences.zh: 你说，快点，我们得选一部电影。

sentences.en: And what will they tell you, Kim?
sentences.zh: 金，他们会跟你说什么？

sentences.en: I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: There are too many for me to choose.
sentences.zh: 选择太多了，我选不出来。

sentences.en: Yeah, I know.
sentences.zh: 是啊，我知道。

sentences.en: I know you say to them, but we got to make a decision.
sentences.zh: 我知道你对他们说，但我们必须做个决定。

sentences.en: What will they again tell you?
sentences.zh: 他们又会跟你说什么？

sentences.en: Well, what's the next one that's playing?
sentences.zh: 嗯，下一场放映的是什么？

sentences.en: Let's go see that.
sentences.zh: 我们去看那部吧。

sentences.en: Oh, that's good.
sentences.zh: 哦，那不错。

sentences.en: That's decisive.
sentences.zh: 那很果断。

sentences.en: No, they're too indecisive.
sentences.zh: 不，他们太优柔寡断了。

sentences.en: We'll say, well, geez, I don't know.
sentences.zh: 他们会说，天哪，我不知道。

sentences.en: I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: They all look good.
sentences.zh: 看起来都不错。

sentences.en: And then you say, well, I chose last time.
sentences.zh: 然后你说，好吧，上次是我选的。

sentences.en: And they'll say, well, that's okay.
sentences.zh: 他们会说，嗯，那没关系。

sentences.en: And then you look at your watch and you say, you know, it's a seven o'clock and they're all starting in 10 minutes.
sentences.zh: 然后你看了看表说，你知道，现在七点了，它们都要在10分钟后开场了。

sentences.en: Which one?
sentences.zh: 选哪一部？

sentences.en: So you make the decision.
sentences.zh: 所以你做了决定。

sentences.en: Now that's brilliant.
sentences.zh: 这招真高明。

sentences.en: Why?
sentences.zh: 为什么？

sentences.en: Well, when you leave the movie, if the movie was good, both of you say nice.
sentences.zh: 嗯，当你离开电影院时，如果电影好看，你们俩都会说不错。

sentences.en: But what if the movie was a stinker?
sentences.zh: 但如果电影很烂呢？

sentences.en: It was a bomb.
sentences.zh: 简直是个灾难。

sentences.en: What will your indecisive friend say to you?
sentences.zh: 你那个优柔寡断的朋友会怎么对你说？

sentences.en: Your fault.
sentences.zh: 都怪你。

sentences.en: You chose it.
sentences.zh: 是你选的。

sentences.en: Why did you make me waste that money?
sentences.zh: 你为什么要让我浪费那笔钱？

sentences.en: Why did you do this?
sentences.zh: 你为什么要这么做？

sentences.en: See?
sentences.zh: 看到了吗？

sentences.en: So they never come across bad.
sentences.zh: 所以他们永远不会显得糟糕。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: They never come across as, you know, a poor decision impacting.
sentences.zh: 他们永远不会表现得像是一个做出糟糕决定的人。

sentences.en: So indecision is a very clever strategy that people will use.
sentences.zh: 所以优柔寡断是人们使用的一种非常聪明的策略。

sentences.en: If I never make the choice, I can never be blamed.
sentences.zh: 如果我从不做选择，我就永远不会被指责。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: If I didn't pick the car, it's not my fault.
sentences.zh: 如果我没选那辆车，那不是我的错。

sentences.en: If I didn't choose the dining room table, it's not my fault.
sentences.zh: 如果我没选那张餐桌，那不是我的错。

sentences.en: I didn't want that refrigerator anyway.
sentences.zh: 反正我本来就不想要那个冰箱。

sentences.en: The problem is indecisives have to realize that, okay, you have the right not to decide.
sentences.zh: 问题是，优柔寡断的人必须意识到，好吧，你有权不决定。

sentences.en: But if someone else made that decision, I'm from New York, we would say, shut up.
sentences.zh: 但如果别人做了那个决定，我是纽约人，我们会说，闭嘴。

sentences.en: You know, we would say, come on.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们会说，得了吧。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: You had the choice.
sentences.zh: 你本来有选择权的。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And you chose not to.
sentences.zh: 而你选择了不选。

sentences.en: And you have every right not to make the decision.
sentences.zh: 你有权不做决定。

sentences.en: You let me do it.
sentences.zh: 你让我来做。

sentences.en: You empowered me.
sentences.zh: 你赋予了我权力。

sentences.en: Then you live with it.
sentences.zh: 那就得接受结果。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: In terms of clutter, the person who is cluttered is very indecisive.
sentences.zh: 就杂物堆积而言，杂物堆积的人非常优柔寡断。

sentences.en: And that makes sense.
sentences.zh: 这说得通。

sentences.en: If I don't choose whether to keep it or not, okay, and I let somebody else finally say, we're getting rid of it.
sentences.zh: 如果我不选择是否保留它，好吧，我让别人最终说，我们把它扔掉吧。

sentences.en: If in the rare time, it's something, you know, nine months later, I wish we had that.
sentences.zh: 如果偶尔有那么一次，你知道，九个月后，我希望我们当时留着它。

sentences.en: Well, you throw it out.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你把它扔了。

sentences.en: You know, I didn't make that decision.
sentences.zh: 你知道，那决定不是我做的。

sentences.en: So, you never come across looking bad.
sentences.zh: 所以，你永远不会显得很糟糕。

sentences.en: So, there's lots of relationship.
sentences.zh: 所以，这之间有很多联系。

sentences.en: So, we've looked at, you know, indecision and clutter.
sentences.zh: 我们研究了优柔寡断和杂物堆积。

sentences.en: We've looked at in the workplace, what impact people in the office who tend to be more indecisive, who also have more office clutter.
sentences.zh: 我们研究了在职场中，那些更优柔寡断、办公桌杂物更多的人会产生什么影响。

sentences.en: Just a whole bunch of them.
sentences.zh: 有一大堆这样的研究。

sentences.en: We've probably got about 20 pubs, 18, 20 pubs now.
sentences.zh: 我们大概已经发表了20篇，18到20篇论文了。

sentences.en: But yeah, no, fascinating.
sentences.zh: 但是，真的，太迷人了。

sentences.en: I like to go into areas where others haven't done any research.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢进入别人还没做过研究的领域。

sentences.en: That's why I started in 88, 89 on the first studies on procrastination, some of the first, because there was nothing in the field.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么我在88、89年开始了关于拖延症的第一批研究，因为当时这个领域一片空白。

sentences.en: Let's see if we can wind up with a question regarding what you're working on now.
sentences.zh: 让我们看看能不能以一个关于你目前工作的问题来结束。

sentences.en: What are the big questions that you would like to be able to answer?
sentences.zh: 你最想回答的重大问题是什么？

sentences.en: I'm doing more than just looking at clutter myself right now.
sentences.zh: 我现在做的不仅仅是关注杂物堆积。

sentences.en: I have a graduate student, and she's looking at what kinds of resources in communities are there for senior citizens.
sentences.zh: 我有一位研究生，她正在研究社区里有哪些资源可以提供给老年人。

sentences.en: That's going to be her doctoral dissertation.
sentences.zh: 那将是她的博士论文。

sentences.en: She's been studying as part of community psych.
sentences.zh: 她一直在社区心理学框架下进行研究。

sentences.en: What are the resources?
sentences.zh: 有哪些资源？

sentences.en: How do we empower people?
sentences.zh: 我们如何赋能于人？

sentences.en: Another one of my students who is an international student from Malta, he's looking at what is the meaning of psychological home, the meaning of home
sentences.zh: 我的另一位学生，他是来自马耳他的国际学生，他正在研究心理家园的意义，家的意义

sentences.en: for migrants and immigrants, particularly immigrant students.
sentences.zh: 对于移民和外来者，特别是移民学生来说是什么。

sentences.en: You're coming here for a short period of time, and you're studying, what does home mean to you?
sentences.zh: 你来到这里待上一小段时间，你在学习，家对你意味着什么？

sentences.en: How does it change?
sentences.zh: 它如何改变？

sentences.en: What does it impact?
sentences.zh: 它有什么影响？

sentences.en: Very exciting study that I'm starting to do is in rural healthcare.
sentences.zh: 我正在开展一项非常令人兴奋的研究，是关于农村医疗保健的。

sentences.en: There's an organization called St. Mary's Clinic that serves people in Kentucky and Tennessee, in Appalachia.
sentences.zh: 有一个叫圣玛丽诊所的组织，服务于肯塔基州和田纳西州阿巴拉契亚地区的人们。

sentences.en: And this fall, I was blessed to have the opportunity to go on a trip through a group called Catholic
sentences.zh: 今年秋天，我有幸通过一个叫“天主教扩展”的组织参加了一次旅行。

sentences.en: Extension.
sentences.zh: 扩展。

sentences.en: And so, one of the things we saw was this big mobile health clinic that goes around to people in Appalachia.
sentences.zh: 我们看到的一件事就是这个大型移动医疗诊所，它在阿巴拉契亚地区四处巡回。

sentences.en: You know, I mean, you know the mobile homes that people buy and the sides come out?
sentences.zh: 你知道，你知道人们买的那种侧面可以展开的移动房屋吗？

sentences.en: Well, imagine that where you've got two examining rooms and a pharmacy and offices in there, all this in this mobile unit.
sentences.zh: 嗯，想象一下那个空间里有两个检查室、一个药房和办公室，所有这些都在这个移动单元里。

sentences.en: And so, they'll go to and deal with 400 patients that are in rural settings.
sentences.zh: 所以，他们会去那里处理农村地区的400名患者。

sentences.en: So, I'm looking at, as a community psychologist, and I have a doctoral student looking at this, what are the needs of those communities?
sentences.zh: 所以，作为一名社区心理学家，我正在研究，我还有一名博士生也在研究这个，这些社区的需求是什么？

sentences.en: Let's evaluate the program.
sentences.zh: 让我们评估一下这个项目。

sentences.en: I'm trying to get my university's nursing and healthcare professions, I'm in the College of Science and
sentences.zh: 我正在努力让我的大学护理和医疗保健专业，我在科学与健康学院，

sentences.en: Health, involved with doing this.
sentences.zh: 参与到这项工作中来。

sentences.en: You know, we're in an urban setting in Chicago, but there are rural needs too.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们身处芝加哥的城市环境，但农村也有需求。

sentences.en: So, we're doing assessments of that.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们正在对此进行评估。

sentences.en: I just love all those guys.
sentences.zh: 我真的很喜欢那些人。

sentences.en: There's so many questions that we are out there to ask that improve the quality of life for people.
sentences.zh: 我们有很多问题需要去探索，以改善人们的生活质量。

sentences.en: And that's what we need to be doing.
sentences.zh: 而这正是我们需要做的。

sentences.en: So, I spent a lot of time early in my career doing work on procrastination, but always did work in community psych, blood donating, litter.
sentences.zh: 所以我职业生涯早期花了很多时间研究拖延症，但也一直从事社区心理学工作，比如献血、乱扔垃圾等。

sentences.en: I have the only studies to get people to buckle up their children in shopping carts, buckle up your baby.
sentences.zh: 我是唯一做过研究，让人们给购物车里的孩子系好安全带的人，给你的宝宝系好安全带。

sentences.en: Yeah, 23,000 kids are in shopping cart accidents.
sentences.zh: 是的，有23000名儿童在购物车事故中受伤。

sentences.en: Then I had NIH grants looking at a wonderful concept with a colleague called Oxford House for people in recovery from substance abuse and alcoholism.
sentences.zh: 后来我获得了NIH的资助，与一位同事研究了一个很棒的概念，叫“牛津之家”，专门针对从药物滥用和酗酒中康复的人。

sentences.en: It's a live-in
sentences.zh: 这是一个居住型的

sentences.en: 12-step, if you would.
sentences.zh: 12步计划，如果你愿意的话。

sentences.en: No therapist, no training.
sentences.zh: 没有治疗师，没有培训。

sentences.en: And yet, we found 85% of the people stay clean and sober two years later.
sentences.zh: 然而，我们发现85%的人在两年后仍然保持清醒和戒断状态。

sentences.en: Most treatment programs, you're lucky if you get 10%.
sentences.zh: 大多数治疗项目，能有10%的成功率就算幸运了。

sentences.en: I did that for 13 years.
sentences.zh: 我做了13年。

sentences.en: So, lots of questions.
sentences.zh: 所以，有很多问题。

sentences.en: I think that's the joy of being an academic.
sentences.zh: 我认为这就是作为学者的乐趣所在。

sentences.en: You can ask lots of questions in lots of different areas.
sentences.zh: 你可以在许多不同的领域提出许多问题。

sentences.en: And I just ask my colleagues, I love basic research.
sentences.zh: 我只是告诉我的同事，我热爱基础研究。

sentences.en: I'm trained as an experimental social, but also, let's make a difference and leave a legacy and make a difference in other people's lives.
sentences.zh: 我受过实验社会心理学的训练，但同时，让我们做出改变，留下遗产，并在他人的生活中产生影响。

sentences.en: I hope this podcast has done that for your listeners.
sentences.zh: 我希望这期播客对你的听众有所帮助。

sentences.en: I hope some people have heard some, among all my ramblings, some kernel of information that they can use to make their life a little bit better.
sentences.zh: 我希望有些人能在我的唠叨中，听到一些他们可以用来让生活变得更好一点的信息核心。

sentences.en: I think you did achieve that.
sentences.zh: 我想你确实做到了。

sentences.en: I want to thank you,
sentences.zh: 我要感谢你，

sentences.en: Dr. Ferrari, for joining me.
sentences.zh: 法拉利博士，感谢你参与我的节目。

sentences.en: And it's been a lot of fun and really interesting.
sentences.zh: 这过程非常有趣，也很有意义。

sentences.en: So, thank you so much.
sentences.zh: 所以，非常感谢你。

sentences.en: Thank you for having me.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你邀请我。

sentences.en: It's good to be had.
sentences.zh: 能被邀请是我的荣幸。
